description: Korean fantasy fiction with stable monarchy, nobility, military, knight, magic, progression, and fantasy-world terminology.

style: Natural, polished English fantasy prose faithful to the Korean source.
Preserve narrator voice, humor, characterization, hierarchy, and shifts between courtly, military, and casual registers.
Use clear English fantasy terminology without mechanically romanizing names that represent European-style people or institutions.
terminology_preservation_rules: Keep recurring royal titles, noble ranks, court offices, military ranks and units, knight orders, magic, mana mechanics, progression ranks, species, artifacts, weapons, skills, techniques, and system terms stable.
Distinguish formal named concepts from ordinary vocabulary and reject generic objects, actions, and one-off descriptions.
Preserve mechanically distinct progression and magic concepts rather than collapsing them into generic levels, ranks, power, or mana.
translation_policy.pinyin_preference: Do not apply Chinese pinyin policy. Korean personal and place names use calibrated romanization, while fantasy-European names should use natural canonical-looking English spellings supported by context rather than mechanical Korean romanization.
translation_policy.semantic_translation_preference: Prefer natural semantic English for descriptive institutions, titles, military formations, magic, skills, and artifacts where the source supports it; preserve established or calibrated proper-name spellings consistently.

terminology_distinctions: Keep royal and noble titles distinct from knight or magical progression ranks.
Keep mana structures, spell terminology, skills, and named techniques mechanically distinct.
Treat fantasy-European proper names as calibrated names, not automatic Korean transliterations.

review_priorities: Royal, noble, court, military, and knight hierarchies.
Mana structures, magic, spells, skills, techniques, and progression ranks.
Organizations, factions, locations, species, named artifacts, and weapons.
Formal songs, poems, and system-like labels when recurring.
Reject generic vocabulary, ordinary objects, and one-off descriptions.

priorities: Royal, noble, court, military, and knight hierarchy consistency.
Magic, mana, spell, skill, technique, and progression terminology.
Organizations, factions, locations, species, artifacts, and weapons.
Formal song, poem, and system-display titles.
Register consistency across courtly, military, comic, and intimate scenes.
Residual Hangul or Korean source script in reader-facing English.
